title: Boltzmann's entropy increase was 'almost always'
summary: The MacTutor biography records Boltzmann's claim that entropy increases almost always, not strictly always.
body: The MacTutor biography of Ludwig Boltzmann, by J. J. O'Connor and E. F. Robertson, says Boltzmann asserted that entropy increases almost always, rather than always, and that he took Poincaré's recurrence result to be theoretically correct but practically irrelevant. That is the careful statistical reading. The v1 slogan "everything tends toward disorder" is looser: the second law, in this reading, is about isolated systems and about what is overwhelmingly likely, and it allows local order when entropy is exported. The MacTutor page is a secondary biography, not Boltzmann's 1877 paper.
